### Preferences

- Writing preference: do not use em-dashes (—) in prose. Prefer periods, semicolons, commas, or parentheses instead. Applies to bios, copy, and any user-facing writing.
- General-purpose embeddings are unsuitable for rhetorical/pragmatic intent classification; topical similarity bias affects all such systems.
- Software engineer building sift, a local semantic search engine and AI agent memory system
- Prefers Rust for systems programming
- Interested in AI agent memory persistence and knowledge graph architectures
- Uses Claude Code as primary development tool


### Corrections

- On 2026-04-04, a stale local-scoped MCP config (visible via `claude mcp get sift`) was pointing to target/debug/sift instead of the installed binary, causing persistent connection failures. `claude mcp remove sift -s local` fixed it.
- Claude Code MCP config precedence: local (project-private) > project (.mcp.json) > user (~/.claude.json). A stale local config silently overrides global fixes.
- The `/mcp` slash command only retries stale connections — it does not re-read config. A full Claude Code restart is required after config changes.


### Decisions

- [Cortex agent reasoning layer] Cortex Phase 1 episode processing uses rule-based extraction only (no LLM). It captures file paths, bash commands, tool metadata, and self-correction language — but cannot extract semantic workflow insights like 'update CHANGELOG before release'. Important procedural knowledge must be stored explicitly via sift_remember.
- [sift] v0.1.6 adds LLM-powered observation extraction in Cortex consolidation — opt-in via llm_extraction config, supports Anthropic/OpenAI/Ollama providers
- [Cortex agent reasoning layer] cortex-workflows.md rule file is NOT useful in its current form. Tool sequence patterns (Bash->Edit->Bash) are generic to all Rust development and add tokens without signal. The other three rule files (decisions, preferences, corrections) carry real value.
- [Cortex agent reasoning layer] Consider either disabling skill_extraction for workflows or improving extraction to capture semantic context about what each tool call did (would require LLM, breaking zero-cost principle).
- [Cortex agent reasoning layer] Full MCP E2E test passes 33/33 checks: remember, recall, list_entities, get_entity, search_skills, forget, consolidate, prune, forget_entity, generate-rules.
- [sift] v0.1.7 highlights: cross-client memory (memory-tool adapter, integrate parity across 9 platforms), typed embedding model registry (9 models with runtime/license/pooling metadata), MCP Streamable HTTP transport ships in release binary, Codex hook parity for sift integrate codex, legacy nomic-embed-text-v2 directories auto-resolve via alias
- [Cortex LLM extraction] Three providers supported: anthropic (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), openai (OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL), ollama (OLLAMA_HOST)
- [sift] Release tarball now includes bash/zsh/fish shell completions in complete/ directory
- [Cortex agent reasoning layer] generate-rules now outputs both AGENTS.md (universal, 20+ tools) and .claude/rules/ (Claude Code native). Detection: .claude/ dir exists = write both, otherwise AGENTS.md only.
- [Cortex agent reasoning layer] CodingMem v0.3.0 benchmark: 95.6% judge score across 92 questions, 8 categories including new proactive category (90.0%).
- [sift] Current version: v0.1.7 (released 2026-04-23) — supersedes the v0.1.6 fact recorded on 2026-04-19
- [Cortex LLM extraction] Heuristic fallback was deleted entirely — the quality gap was too large to justify maintaining both paths
- [Cortex LLM extraction] Haiku 4.5 achieves 100% accuracy on 19-sentence test set with perfect skip detection at ~$0.003/session
- [sift] Homebrew tap is live: brew install raymondj99/tap/sift. Release CI auto-pushes formula updates via HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN secret
- [sift] v0.1.6 removes heuristic extraction (substring markers, correction language detection, 500-char truncation) from PostCompact and Stop episodes — LLM-only now
- [sift] Full workspace test suite at v0.1.7 release: 926 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored across 12 crates
- [sift] v0.1.7 release binary size: 15.99 MB with RELEASE_FEATURES='standard,mcp,mcp-http,serve,completions' — 36% headroom under 25 MB threshold. mcp-http cost was only +0.51 MB because axum/tower-http mostly share deps with the already-linked tokio/hyper stack from sift-server
- [local vs remote lock file sync] cargo deny check passing locally doesn't guarantee CI pass if the committed lock file diverges from local state due to prior cargo update not being committed.
- [rand dependency RUSTSEC-2026-0002] CI failed because advisory ignore was removed from deny.toml but Cargo.lock on remote still had vulnerable rand 0.8.5; local Cargo.lock had been updated to 0.8.6 separately but not committed.
- [RAC EMA centroid classifier] Adaptive embedding classifier approach was abandoned after PoC revealed only 26% accuracy; embeddings cluster by topic rather than intent.
- [CI jobs clippy lints] Clippy job was failing with 7 lints from Rust 1.95; addressed by commits in CI run `24621006914`.
- [rebuild_lock race condition] RwLock barrier prevents concurrent recall from observing half-rebuilt vector index; write lock during rebuild, read lock during recall prevents data corruption.
- [unknown_lints warning] First commit landed with `unknown_lints` warning because pre-commit hooks didn't block it; CI caught the issue.
- [rand dependency] Bumped `rand` to 0.8.6 to resolve RUSTSEC-2026-0097 vulnerability flagged by deny job.
- [deny RUSTSEC-2026-0097 rand] Updated rand from 0.8.5 to 0.8.6 via cargo update to patch ThreadRng unsoundness vulnerability.
- [API timeout handling] Without CONNECT_TIMEOUT (5s) and CALL_TIMEOUT (30s), hung endpoints could stall the daemon indefinitely; timeouts implemented via shared ureq::Agent built once per llm_decompose call.
- [pre-commit hooks clippy] Pre-commit hooks run `cargo clippy` without `-D warnings`, allowing commits with warnings that CI later rejects with `-D warnings` flag.
- [clippy 1.95 map_unwrap_or] Fixed map_unwrap_or lint violations in onnx.rs:51 and main.rs:102 on Result types.
- [clippy 1.95 collapsible_match] Fixed collapsible_match lint violations in consolidation.rs:695, epub.rs:137, office.rs:113, and office.rs:218.
- [CI clippy configuration] CI uses `-D warnings` flag for clippy, enforcing strict linting as final gate before merge.
- [Cortex automated memory system] Cortex is sift's automated memory system — dual-path architecture with hot-path encoding (Claude Code hooks, <100ms, zero LLM cost) and cold-path consolidation (daemon background, 5-phase pipeline using local embeddings)


### Workflows

- Formula renamed from sift to sift-search because homebrew-core already has a sift formula (grep-like tool by Sven Taute, v0.9.1). Install command: brew install raymondj99/tap/sift-search
- Formula declares conflicts_with "sift" so Homebrew will warn if both are installed
- Release CI generates sift-search.rb (class SiftSearch) and pushes to raymondj99/homebrew-tap
- Before deploying any release, always verify the binary size stays under 25MB.
- The process is: build release binary, check with stat, compare against threshold.
- Remember to run the benchmark suite after any search scoring changes.
- Dependency: embedding model must be available during consolidation (already required for dedup in Phase 2)
- Always add to CHANGELOG.md when landing features, not just at release time.
- When removing advisory ignores from deny.toml, always verify that Cargo.lock in the same commit reflects the patched dependency version before pushing.
